consensus_summary: Primary consensus identifies 'poor, meek, needy' as the anawim: humble faithful who recognize spiritual poverty and total dependence on God (vs. proud/self-sufficient), inheriting kingdom/earth; material readings are common alternatives but secondary/overlapping.
book_summary: Those bowed and empty-handed before God, receptive to what the self-sufficient refuse; they hear the gospel and inherit the kingdom (opposite: rich).
consensus_core_identification: Humble/dependent faithful (anawim) characterized by spiritual poverty, meekness, and trust in God rather than self.
book_core_identification: Those bowed/empty-handed before God (receptive vs. self-sufficient) who hear the gospel and inherit the kingdom.
boundary_disagreement: None material; book’s explicit opposite (‘rich’/self-sufficient) and receptivity focus align with consensus primary without excluding its overlapping material connotations or adding new cases.
rationale: Both cores name the same referent: the humble who depend on God and receive what the proud refuse. Book wording (‘bowed and empty-handed… able to receive’) is a direct paraphrase of the anawim/spiritual-poverty consensus culminating in the Beatitudes; shared citations and kingdom-inheritance outcome confirm equivalence. Extra consensus detail (literal poverty alternatives, remnant history, gentleness virtue) is immaterial to the core match.
strongest_objection: Book’s silence on explicit socioeconomic readings might be read as narrowing, yet this does not alter the shared primary core or create contradiction.
